title: Agent wallets compared

guidance.text: Agentic Mobile Protocol uses user signed mandates that Intent Guard checks before payment. Wallet controls cover task visibility, delegation limits and disputes.

Pick Binance Agentic Wallet if you need separate daily limits for transactions, prediction trades, DeFi, Developer Mode signing, and x402. The settings page says the CLI can read those limits and that settings can only be changed in the Binance App.

Pick ChatGPT Wallet if you need a saved card a dot can spend after the user reviews the items, total, and selected card and approves with Face ID, Touch ID, or a fingerprint scan. The payment network then provides a payment token charged to that card.
Pick Circle Agent Wallets if you need USDC transfer caps for a transaction, a day, a week, and a month. Setting a policy sends an email one time password.
Coinbase is retiring Agentic Wallet and points new agent wallet setups to Coinbase Wallet MCP, a separate wallet. Funds in the old wallet must be withdrawn before 15 January 2027.
guidance.source_title: Coinbase developer docs index, Migrate to Wallet MCP section

guidance.text: Pick Coinbase Wallet MCP if you need an assistant connected to Coinbase Wallet, with each write approved in that wallet and an x402 maxPayment cap in USDC. The approval mode page says that mode is the only execution mode today.

Pick Coinstancy Agentic Bank if you need a USDC wallet on Base with budgets per payment, per day, and per month, plus an approval threshold and a frozen flag. The developer docs say pay_x402 is disabled by default.

Pick Fireblocks Agentic Payments Suite if you need Agent Wallets with scoped, revocable spending authority. The 20 May 2026 blog states per wallet and per delegation rules for spend limits, merchant allowlists, time windows, and asset constraints.
guidance.source_title: Fireblocks Powers an Agentic Payments Future for PSPs and Fintechs

guidance.text: Pick Hedera Agent Accounts if you need an owner funded spending account with a daily cap and a per transaction maximum. The 8 October 2026 post states those limits, payment in HBAR or USDC, and a mainnet target of Q2 2027.
Pick Kite Agent Passport if you need a passkey approved session on a wallet funded in USDC.e. The payments page states a per transaction maximum, a total budget, and x402 pricing for the paid call.

Pick Lightspark Agent Accounts if you need an agent to spend from a self-custodial Global Account the customer owns. Grid enforces per transaction, daily, and monthly limits, and it can hold a payment for approval.
Pick MetaMask Agent Wallet if you need Guard Mode allowlists and a rolling 24 hour outflow limit with 2FA outside that policy. The trading modes page states those controls.

Pick Polygon Agent CLI if you need an embedded wallet that pays x402 under a stated per call cap. The CLI reference says the default per call limit is $1 and the rolling 24 hour total is $10, and session logout revokes that install.

Pick Shop MCP if you need a card issued for one approved purchase. The approvals page says Shop gives the agent card details paid by the saved card, approval_limit is the most that card can be charged, and cancel does not revoke a card already issued.

Pick Skyfire if you need a pay token whose amount is the maximum a seller can charge against a buyer wallet. The tokenAmount page states that maximum and says it cannot exceed the buyer agent wallet balance.

Pick Stabletrust API if you need a hosted transfer API that sends the agent private key. The API page says to fund a dedicated agent wallet with only what the agent needs, because that key travels with every request.

Pick Stripe link-cli if you need a funded Link balance that can skip approval under a per purchase limit. The support page says the user sets that limit, purchases above it still need approval, and a limit of $0 prevents skipping.
guidance.source_title: Set up a balance for agent wallet purchases

guidance.text: Pick Stripe Treasury for agents if you need a Treasury account through MCP where live money movement waits for approval. The docs mark the money movement tools Public preview and say approval is the default.
Pick Tempo Wallet if you need an MPP payment under a max spend cap. The recipes page says the max spend flag caps one command, and access key limits apply separately to the signing key.
Visa CLI lets agents pay per request APIs and earn task rewards in OUSD on Tempo within limits the owner sets.

Pick Wavelength if you need a self-custodial Lightning wallet an agent can drive over MCP, with no node or channels to run. The 23 October 2026 post says mainnet is open to everyone as an alpha, and L402 pays per request.
guidance.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

custody.text: The FAQ says Binance Agentic Wallet is a dedicated keyless wallet created under the Binance account. It has its own isolated balance, and the main wallet is unaffected. The FAQ says it is built on an MPC wallet.

settlement.text: The wallet chains example lists BNB Smart Chain, Ethereum, Solana, Base, Arbitrum One, Polygon, and Robinhood.

protocols.text: x402-payment preview reads a PAYMENT-REQUIRED payload, and x402-payment sign signs one option. Only x402 v2 is supported, and only on BSC, Base, and Solana. Ethereum is not supported for x402. A payment is not signable with BLOCKED_DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED when the x402 daily limit is used. The page does not name MPP, AP2, or ACP.

spend_limits.text: The settings page states a daily limit on total transaction value per 24 hours, plus separate daily limits for prediction trades, DeFi operations, Developer Mode external signing, and x402 payments. When tradeAllTokens is off, the wallet trades only tokens on an allowed list. abnormalTxnHandling is AutoReject or NeedConfirmation. NeedConfirmation sends a double confirm request to the Binance App. Settings can only be changed in the Binance App.

human_approval.text: The FAQ says the owner confirms the pairing code in the Binance App at sign in. It says Secure Auto Sign, once authorized, allows transactions to execute without individual transaction confirmations.

custody.text: The help article says ChatGPT Wallet stores the card details. After approval, the payment network provides a payment token with a card number, security code, and expiration date, and the payment is charged to the selected card without sharing the actual card details with the business or the agent.

settlement.text: The announcement says the payment is charged to the selected card. The help article says eligible cards are US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard, and Visa credit cards. Debit cards are not supported. Virtual cards are not supported at launch. This is separate from the virtual card number Wallet uses to complete an approved purchase.

protocols.text: The accept payments guide says no Wallet-specific website integration is required and merchants receive a network token, not the full card number. They can use the Payment Account Reference to associate the token with the underlying payment account. The announcement tells businesses to recognize signed requests using Web Bot Auth.

human_approval.text: Before each purchase the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves with a security check such as Face ID, Touch ID, or a fingerprint scan on a supported device. Saving a card and approving a purchase are separate steps.

revocation.text: The help article says removing a saved card means it cannot be used for new Wallet payments unless added back. Removal does not cancel purchases, close the card with the bank, or delete Wallet data or the OpenAI account. The help article does not describe a way to stop an already approved payment that is still in progress.

custody.text: The agent wallet guide says an agent's wallet on Tempo is an access key the agent generates and holds. The account signers authorize that key. The page says not to give the agent the account key.

settlement.text: The guide's spending limit example is 50 of a stablecoin a day, and the code comment calls that amount 50 OUSD. The same page says the interactive demo pays test AlphaUSD on the Tempo Accounts devnet.

protocols.text: The pay with the CLI guide says the CLI handles the MPP challenge and payment retry. It does not name x402, AP2, ACP, or MCP.
protocols.source_title: Tempo guide to paying with the CLI

spend_limits.text: The recipes page says the max spend flag caps one command's payment spending, and access key limits apply separately to the signing key.

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The agent wallet guide says the account signers authorize the access key. It does not state a later approval above a spend threshold.

revocation.text: The agent wallet guide says the signers revoke the key by its saved address.

status.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The agent wallet guide does not call Tempo Wallet generally available, beta, or preview. It says that until T14, a configurable account can authorize an agent key only on the devnet.

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-29. The wallet recipes page does not name a software license or a price.

custody.text: The Turnkey case study says Visa CLI is non-custodial: the owner's wallet and the keys that move it sit in the owner's own Turnkey account.
custody.source_title: Case study: Visa CLI on Turnkey

settlement.text: Agents earn task rewards in OUSD on Tempo.

protocols.text: Per request APIs return HTTP 402 with a charge on Tempo.

spend_limits.text: The owner signs one authorization on Tempo that sets what the agent can spend, and Tempo applies that limit on chain.
spend_limits.source_title: Case study: Visa CLI on Turnkey

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-23.

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-23.

status.text: Beta. Access is by invitation only.
status.source_title: Visa CLI status: what's live today

license.text: Not documented as of 2026-11-23.

custody.text: The system page says the client holds the user's keys and signs payments. The coordination service never has unilateral control of funds, and exit moves the balance back to the Bitcoin blockchain without anyone's permission.

settlement.text: The 23 October 2026 post says humans and agents can pay and get paid in bitcoin over Lightning, with stablecoins coming soon.
settlement.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

protocols.text: The 23 October 2026 post says wavecli mcp serve exposes the wallet as MCP tool calls, and L402 charges sats per request with no signup and no API key. It does not name x402, MPP, or AP2.
protocols.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

spend_limits.text: The 23 October 2026 post caps each mainnet account at 300,000 sats and each VTXO at 50,000 sats. It does not state a per agent spend limit, budget, or payee allowlist.
spend_limits.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

human_approval.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-30. The 23 October 2026 post says an agent pays with no human approving each transaction. It does not state approval above a spend threshold.
human_approval.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026

revocation.text: Not documented as of 2026-10-30. The bakemacaroon page can set a client side expiry on a macaroon. It does not document revoking a baked macaroon.

status.text: The 23 October 2026 post says Wavelength is now live on mainnet for everyone and that this is still an alpha.
status.source_title: Lightning Labs: Wavelength on mainnet, 23 October 2026
